Subject: Throughput & Concurrency: Dedicated Capacity Sizing — decision checkpoints

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick written recap so we have aligned acceptance criteria for the Dedicated capacity sizing exercise and next steps from our side.

Summary of what we heard from Clara Health:
- Peak concurrent active sessions: ~30 (webapp users creating multi-turn summaries)
- Average tokens per session (per request): ~180 tokens; bursts up to ~600 tokens for long workflows
- Streaming is required: first-token and steady-state token latency matter for perceived UX
- Target SLOs you asked us to validate: 95th pct first-token latency <= 120ms, steady-state token latency <= 25ms/token, and sustained aggregate token throughput of ~10k tokens/sec for daytime peak.

What we'll validate on Dedicated:
1) GPU type tradeoffs (A100 80GB vs H100 vs L4-type inference variant) — cost vs latency/throughput envelope
2) Reserved throughput configuration to meet 30 concurrent sessions with burst headroom (target buffer: +25%)
3) Streaming behavior verification (first-byte latency and steady-state token cadence under concurrency)
4) Failure/fallback behavior: what happens under throttling and graceful degradation to smaller model variant

Immediate next steps (ours):
- We'll run a 48–72 hour comparative run across three GPU configs and produce a throughput/concurrency matrix and recommendation. (Deliverable: throughput_matrix_v2.xlsx)
- Draft a mutual action plan (timeline, milestones, success criteria, procurement steps). (Deliverable: ma_plan_draft.pdf)
- Share the test harness and instructions so your infra team can reproduce results. (Deliverable: gpu_eval_instructions.txt)

Can you confirm the SLO targets above are correct (esp first-token p95 and aggregate token throughput)? If there are adjustments we should incorporate them into the test plan.

I'll loop in Aditya and Ben here for execution.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi — thanks for the recap and the clear next steps. Confirming the SLOs with a couple of clarifications:

- First-token p95 <= 120ms is accurate for interactive flows (our UI is sensitive). For batch exports (scheduled summaries) we're okay with p95 <= 400ms.
- Steady-state 25ms/token is a target but we're flexible to 30ms/token if it buys cost savings.
- Aggregate daytime peak of ~10k tokens/sec is our nominal ask; plan should show headroom to 12–13k for unexpected spikes.

Procurement note: we typically need a one-page technical signoff from vendors before contracts teams will start the procurement paperwork. If you can deliver the MA plan + short perf findings within 5 business days after the run, that will keep our procurement timeline on track.

Also looping Elena from our ML infra team in case she has any implementation-side notes.

—Samir

Rishi / team — plan looks doable. Proposed approach and quick notes:

1) Test bed and config
- Models: rfin-7b-quant and rfin-3b-optimized (to show tradeoffs); we will include a medium-sized reference model to demonstrate headroom on cheaper GPUs.
- GPUs: A100-80GB (fp16 optimized), H100 (tensor core propagation), L4-equivalent (int8 inference profile).
- Synthetic workload: multi-turn chat-like sessions with 180 tokens/request avg, and a separate long-run test at 600 tokens/request for batch.

2) Measurement points
- Concurrency levels: 5, 15, 30, 38
- Metrics: first-byte latency (p50/p95), steady-state token latency (p50/p95), tokens/sec aggregate, and GPU-util/VRAM headroom.

3) Expected turnaround
- Baseline runs per GPU: 8–12 hours each to collect stable metrics + one longer 24-hour soak run on recommended config. Total wall-time: ~72 hours.

I'll produce throughput_matrix_v2.xlsx with a sheet per GPU and a summary tab calling out cost-per-token (estimated). I'll also attach a lightweight test harness instructions file (gpu_eval_instructions.txt) so Clara's infra can reproduce.

Quick notes from infra/ops perspective:
- H100 will almost certainly hit the first-token p95 target at 30 concurrency for the rfin-7b-quant model, but cost will be ~1.6x vs A100 for the same reservation.
- A100-80GB is the most predictable for steady-state token cadence because of larger VRAM headroom (fewer KV cache evictions). For 30 concurrency I expect slightly higher p95 first-token than H100 but within the 120–140ms range; that's borderline.
- L4-equivalent is fine for the 3b optimized model and will be the best cost-per-token if Clara is willing to accept slightly higher first-byte latency for the interactive flow (we can show this in the matrix).
- Recommendation: run A100 and L4 runs first; if A100 p95 is >130ms at 30 concurrency we should prioritize a quick H100 run for contrast.

I'll instrument the harness to collect GPU-level counters and add a short note on autoscale/fallback behavior for the MA plan.
